title: Super Washing Machines
summary: In one simultaneous move, any nonempty set of machines may each send ONE dress to ONE adjacent machine.
statement: In one simultaneous move, any nonempty set of machines may each send ONE dress to ONE adjacent machine. A machine cannot send to both neighbors in one move. A machine may receive from both neighbors and may send a dress it already held while receiving. An initially empty machine cannot forward a newly received dress in that same move. Return the minimum moves to equalize every load; return -1 if the total is not divisible by the number of machines. Already equal loads need zero moves.
constraints: 1 <= machines.length <= 10,000; each load is an integer from 0 to 100,000.

A machine may receive from both neighbors and may send a dress it already held while receiving. An initially empty machine cannot forward a newly received dress in that same move.
Return the minimum moves to equalize every load; return -1 if the total is not divisible by the number of machines. Already equal loads need zero moves.
reference_solution:
def minimum_washing_moves(machines):
    total=sum(machines);n=len(machines)
    if total%n:return -1
    average=total//n;balance=best=0
    for count in machines:
        surplus=count-average;balance+=surplus
        best=max(best,abs(balance),surplus)
    return best

hints: The target load must be the integer average; every prefix has a net surplus or deficit.
Each edge must carry the absolute prefix imbalance. Also, a machine can send at most one of its own surplus dresses per round.
Accumulate balance += load-average and update answer with abs(balance) and load-average. Reject indivisible totals first.
Do not take the absolute value of the local surplus: receiving from two sides can happen together, but sending to two sides needs separate rounds.
editorial: Conservation fixes the net flow across each edge to the prefix imbalance, giving a lower bound of its absolute value. If a machine supplies both sides, its outgoing requirements add to load-average, another lower bound because it sends at most one dress per round. Otherwise flows can pass through in parallel while receiving. On a line, these directed flows can be pipelined, meeting the maximum of the edge and combined-outgoing bottlenecks; no per-round simulation is needed. The independent oracle instead performs BFS over load vectors and enumerates every simultaneous legal send choice from the pre-move state. It shares no prefix-bound calculation with the reference.

tests.explanation: Three simultaneous rounds suffice: [1,0,5] → [1,1,4] → [2,1,3] → [2,2,2]. The last machine must send its three excess dresses in separate rounds.
Return 1: both ends send one dress to the middle simultaneously, producing [2,2,2]. Receiving two dresses at once is allowed; sending two is not.
